stories.title: Supreme Court signals it will send the Krishna Janmabhoomi-Shahi Idgah 'who represents Hindus' dispute back to the Allahabad High Court
key_points: The Supreme Court said it is **inclined to remand** a key procedural fight in the long-running Krishna Janmabhoomi-Shahi Idgah case back to the **Allahabad High Court**.
The dispute is over **which plaintiffs get to represent** 'all devotees of Lord Krishna' in the underlying suit — not the core temple-mosque dispute itself.
The High Court had let one Hindu party (suit no. 17) represent all devotees **without formally notifying** the plaintiffs from other, earlier suits, including suit no. 1.
A bench of **Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva** wants all plaintiffs given a fair hearing on the representation question before the case moves forward.
The matter has been adjourned to **September 2** for a formal order.
stories.background: The Krishna Janmabhoomi-Shahi Idgah dispute is one of India's most sensitive ongoing religious-property cases, centred on a mosque in Mathura that Hindu petitioners say sits on the site of Lord Krishna's birthplace, and which some groups want removed or partially reclaimed. It sits alongside the Ayodhya Ram Mandir dispute as one of a handful of major Hindu-Muslim religious site disputes working through India's courts over the past decade, and both sides have long anticipated it could become similarly high-profile. Multiple separate lawsuits by different Hindu petitioner groups have been filed over the years, each claiming to represent devotees' interests — which is what created today's narrower procedural fight over who actually gets to be the 'lead' plaintiff group in court.
stories.what_happened: The Supreme Court was hearing an appeal from plaintiffs in the original 2020 suit (suit no. 1, which seeks removal of the mosque), who challenged an **Allahabad High Court ruling** that let a different, later group of petitioners (suit no. 17) be treated as the representative voice for 'all devotees of Lord Krishna' in the case. The bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva observed that the High Court had made this designation **without issuing notice to the plaintiffs in the other suits**, meaning those parties never got a chance to argue against it. The judges indicated they are inclined to send the representation question back down to the Allahabad High Court so it can be reheard properly, with all plaintiffs given notice and an opportunity to be heard this time. The Court granted an adjournment until **September 2**, when it is expected to formalise this order.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a procedural ruling, not a decision on the underlying temple-mosque dispute — but it matters because it resets who gets to speak for the Hindu side in a case that could eventually decide the fate of a functioning mosque. Getting the representation question wrong risks the eventual final verdict being challenged on fairness grounds.
stories.ripple_effects: The remand likely adds months, possibly longer, to an already slow-moving case, since the Allahabad High Court must now redo this procedural step with proper notice to all parties. It also sets a precedent for how courts handle cases where multiple petitioner groups claim to represent the same community.
stories.why_now: The Supreme Court took up this specific appeal about the representation question during a hearing this week, and its oral remarks signalling an intended remand were reported as they happened.
stories.watch_next: Watch for the Supreme Court's formal order on September 2, and how quickly the Allahabad High Court moves once the matter is sent back.

key_terms.definition: When a higher court sends a case back down to a lower court to be reconsidered, usually because a procedural step was skipped or done incorrectly.

stories.the_lesson: In court cases involving competing groups claiming to represent the same community, procedural fairness — making sure everyone gets notice and a chance to be heard — can end up being just as consequential as the substance of the underlying dispute.

stories.title: Supreme Court slams Karnataka's 'absurd' terror-trial delays, orders a dedicated fast-track court
key_points: The Supreme Court criticized Karnataka's prosecution plan in a **UAPA (terror law) case** as 'absurd'
The accused, Shahid Khan, has been in custody since **September 2022** without trial completing
Of **707 witnesses** in the case, the state proposed examining just 50 in relation to Khan — with no timeline
The Court called it **'callousness'** for the state to keep a citizen jailed without a clear trial plan
It ordered Karnataka to set up an **additional special court** dedicated to UAPA cases within two weeks
stories.background: The UAPA (Unlawful Activities Prevention Act) is India's main anti-terror law, allowing extended pre-trial detention and making bail much harder to get than under ordinary criminal law. Critics have long argued it lets the state keep people in jail for years without ever proving a case in court, effectively making the process itself the punishment. This case involves an accused linked to the **Popular Front of India (PFI)**, an Islamic organisation the government banned in 2022 over alleged extremist links, and the ruling was delivered by a bench led by Chief Justice of India **Surya Kant**.
stories.what_happened: The Supreme Court bench, hearing a bail plea from Shahid Khan — in custody since **September 22, 2022** in a case involving PFI members — pulled up the Karnataka government over what it called an 'absurd' prosecution plan. The state's case involves 707 witnesses in total, but its own submission proposed examining only 50 of them specifically in relation to Khan, with no clear timeline for finishing the trial. The bench said the state cannot have "the luxury of prolonging trial for years" while a citizen sits in jail awaiting trial, calling it "callousness" for a prosecuting agency to withhold a clear picture of when a case will conclude. As a remedy, the Court directed the Karnataka government to set up an **additional special court** to hear UAPA cases exclusively, on a day-to-day basis, with the necessary approvals to be granted within two weeks.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a direct check on how anti-terror law is applied in practice: courts, not just legislators, are pushing back on prosecutions that keep citizens jailed indefinitely without a credible plan to actually try the case. It reinforces a constitutional principle — the right to a fair and timely trial — against a law that has often been criticized for enabling the opposite.
stories.ripple_effects: The ruling could pressure other states with backlogged UAPA cases to speed up trials or risk similar judicial rebukes, and it may bolster bail arguments for other long-detained UAPA-accused individuals citing 'trial delay' as a ground. It also adds to a broader pattern of the current Supreme Court bench taking a firmer line on prolonged pre-trial detention across various laws.
stories.why_now: The ruling came as the Court heard Khan's bail plea after nearly four years in custody, prompting the bench to confront the state directly over the case's lack of progress.
stories.watch_next: Watch for whether Karnataka meets the two-week deadline to set up the new special court, and whether Khan is granted bail as the case proceeds.

key_terms.definition: The Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act — India's principal anti-terrorism law, known for strict bail conditions that let authorities detain accused people for long periods before trial.
The Popular Front of India, an Islamic organisation banned by the Indian government in 2022 over alleged links to extremism and unlawful activity.

stories.the_lesson: A right (like bail or a fair trial) that exists on paper but takes years to enforce in practice isn't much of a right at all — courts stepping in to fix process delays is often as important as the underlying law itself.

stories.title: Pakistan captain Babar Azam retires hurt in a hand injury scare, days before the England Test series begins
key_points: Babar Azam **retired hurt** after being struck on the hand by a **Manny Lumsden** delivery in Pakistan's final warm-up match
Pakistan **collapsed from 164-2 to 238 all out**, surrendering a **67-run first-innings deficit**
The warm-up was against a **PCC Select XI** at **Beckenham**, Pakistan's last hit-out before the **England Test series**
**Abdullah Shafique** top-scored with **61** in the innings
England's **Emilio Gay** made a **pair** in the same match, for a very different reason — form, not injury
stories.background: This is a three-day tour match between Pakistan and a **Professional County Club Select XI** at Beckenham, Pakistan's final preparation game before their full Test series against **England** begins. Pakistan had bowled the home side out for **305** on day one, but were themselves under pressure after collapsing from a strong position in their own first innings.
stories.what_happened: On day two, Pakistan slumped from **164 for 2 to 238 all out**, handing the PCC Select XI a **67-run first-innings lead** after the hosts had made 305. **Abdullah Shafique** was the innings' top scorer with **61**. During the collapse, captain **Babar Azam** was struck on the hand by a delivery from **Manny Lumsden** and **retired hurt**, ruling him out of the rest of this warm-up game and raising doubts over his fitness for the opening Test. On the other side, England's **Emilio Gay**, also using the match to prepare for the Pakistan series, was dismissed for a **duck** in the second innings after edging behind — his second failure of the match. The PCC Select XI reached **128 for 3** in their second innings by stumps, with **Shoaib Bashir** taking 4 for 76 with the ball for the home side.
stories.why_it_matters: Babar Azam is Pakistan's captain and best batter — any doubt over his fitness this close to a Test series against England is a serious concern for the team, on top of an already shaky batting display in the warm-up.
stories.ripple_effects: If Babar is ruled out or has to play carrying an injury, Pakistan's batting order — already fragile in this warm-up — would face even more pressure in a series against a strong England side. It also puts extra scrutiny on Pakistan's other top-order batters to step up.
stories.why_now: The injury happened in Pakistan's final tune-up match before the Test series proper begins, making the timing especially costly.
stories.watch_next: Confirmation of Babar Azam's fitness ahead of the first Test, and whether he's cleared to play or Pakistan need a replacement.

key_terms.definition: When a batter leaves the field due to injury rather than being dismissed — they can return to bat later in the innings if fit.

stories.the_lesson: In cricket, the biggest risk to a team's plans often isn't the opposition — it's an untimely injury to a key player in the days before it matters most.

stories.title: Guyana Amazon Warriors open their CPL 2026 title bid with a comfortable win over Jamaica Kingsmen
key_points: **Guyana Amazon Warriors** bowled out Jamaica Kingsmen for just **117** to open their CPL 2026 campaign.
**Mohammad Nabi** took **4 wickets**, and **Shai Hope's unbeaten 56** sealed the chase.
The win put Guyana **top of the early CPL 2026 table**.
**Jamaica Kingsmen** have now **lost all three** of their matches this season.
stories.background: The Caribbean Premier League is the Caribbean's flagship T20 franchise competition, running annually since 2013 and expanded to **seven teams** for 2026. Guyana Amazon Warriors built a strong overseas contingent this season specifically to chase the title, pairing Caribbean talent with experienced international players like Nabi, Phillips, Tahir and Pretorius.
stories.what_happened: **Guyana Amazon Warriors** began their **Caribbean Premier League (CPL) 2026** campaign with a six-wicket win over **Jamaica Kingsmen** at Sabina Park, Kingston. Put in to bowl first, Guyana bundled Jamaica out for just **117**, with **Mohammad Nabi** returning figures of **4 wickets** to rip through the middle order. Guyana then chased the target down comfortably, with **Shai Hope unbeaten on 56** off 41 balls anchoring the run-chase alongside contributions from Nabi and Quentin Sampson. The result put the Amazon Warriors top of the early CPL table and extended Jamaica Kingsmen's losing run to **three matches** from three this season. Guyana fielded a heavily overseas-stocked squad this year, including Afghanistan all-rounder Nabi, New Zealand's Glenn Phillips, and South Africa's Imran Tahir and Dwaine Pretorius, giving the team an experienced core to build a title push around.
stories.why_it_matters: A dominant opening win, built on both bowling and a calm chase, signals Guyana as an early title contender in a tournament that regularly feeds players into bigger leagues worldwide, including the IPL.
stories.ripple_effects: Jamaica Kingsmen now face mounting pressure to turn their season around after three straight defeats, with their net run rate taking an early hit. Strong individual form from players like Nabi and Hope also raises their profile ahead of upcoming international assignments.
stories.why_now: This was Guyana's tournament-opening match, played this week as the CPL 2026 season got underway.
stories.watch_next: Whether Guyana Amazon Warriors can keep their unbeaten start going as the CPL group stage continues through September.

key_terms.definition: The Caribbean's main T20 franchise cricket tournament, featuring teams representing different Caribbean nations and islands.

stories.the_lesson: In T20 cricket, a strong bowling performance that restricts the opposition often matters more to the result than a flashy batting total — Guyana won this game with the ball, not just the bat.

stories.title: Sunrisers Leeds grind past Southern Brave to reach the Hundred women's final
key_points: **Sunrisers Leeds** beat Southern Brave by **five wickets**, chasing 114/7 with **116/5** and 11 balls in hand.
**Hannah Baker** (2/13) was Player of the Match for a disciplined bowling display.
**Deepti Sharma's unbeaten 28** anchored the chase, with Winfield-Hill making 37.
Sunrisers advance to **Sunday's final at Lord's** to defend their Hundred women's title.
stories.background: The Hundred is England's franchise cricket competition, with eight men's and eight women's teams playing a 100-ball format each August. Sunrisers Leeds are the reigning women's champions and needed a nervy group-stage win over Manchester Super Giants earlier this week just to qualify for the knockout stage, before facing Southern Brave in Friday's winner-takes-all Eliminator at the Oval.
stories.what_happened: Defending champions **Sunrisers Leeds** beat **Southern Brave** by **five wickets** in the Hundred women's Eliminator at the Kennington Oval, chasing down Southern Brave's **114 for 7** with **116 for 5** and 11 balls to spare. **Hannah Baker** took **2 wickets for 13 runs** off her 20 balls and was named Player of the Match for a tight bowling spell that kept the target low. In the chase, **Lauren Winfield-Hill** made **37**, and **Deepti Sharma** anchored the finish with an unbeaten **28** to see Sunrisers home. The win sends Sunrisers Leeds into **Sunday's final** at Lord's, where they will defend the title they won last year. It comes after Sunrisers had already needed a separate win over Manchester Super Giants to even reach this Eliminator, in a tense finish to the group stage this week.
stories.why_it_matters: This sets up the women's final as the marquee finish to the Hundred's 2026 season, with Sunrisers now one win away from defending their title. It also extends the tournament's growing platform for women's franchise cricket in England.
stories.ripple_effects: Southern Brave's elimination ends their season and shifts full attention to whoever they face in the final. Sunrisers' bowlers, particularly Baker, head into the final with momentum after delivering under Eliminator pressure.
stories.why_now: The Eliminator was today's match, the final knockout step before Sunday's title decider.
stories.watch_next: Who Sunrisers Leeds face in Sunday's Hundred women's final at Lord's, and whether they can defend their title.
stories.the_lesson: In knockout cricket, tight, disciplined bowling in the middle overs — not just big individual scores — is often what actually decides a low-scoring chase.

stories.title: Tanzid Hasan's maiden Test century flips Bangladesh from trailing to 153 runs clear against Australia

thread.previously: At stumps on day one in Darwin, Bangladesh had bowled Australia out for just 198 and replied with 96/1, still trailing by 102 runs.
thread.changed: By stumps on day two, Bangladesh piled on runs to reach 351/6 — turning a 102-run deficit into a 153-run lead — with Tanzid Hasan scoring a maiden Test century.

key_points: **Tanzid Hasan** scored **101**, his maiden Test century, on Bangladesh's historic first Test tour of Australia.
He's only the **second Asian batter ever** — after Hanif Mohammad in 1964 — to score a century on a debut tour Down Under.
**Najmul Hossain Shanto** added **84** as Bangladesh reached **351 for 6** at stumps on day two.
Bangladesh have gone from trailing by 102 runs to now leading by **153 runs**.
**Mehidy Hasan Miraz (32*)** and **Hasan Mahmud (13*)** batted out the final overs to protect the lead.
stories.background: Bangladesh had never played a Test match in Australia until this series, ending a **23-year wait** for a tour Down Under — historically one of the hardest places for touring teams to bat. On day one, Bangladesh's bowlers stunned the hosts, dismissing Australia for just 198, before ending the day 96/1 in reply, still 102 runs behind. Test centuries on a first-ever tour of Australia are rare for any team, let alone one still establishing itself in the format.
stories.what_happened: On day two of the first Test in Darwin, Bangladesh's batting lineup built on their day-one bowling performance in dramatic fashion. Opener **Tanzid Hasan** scored **101**, becoming just the second Asian batter in history — after Pakistan's Hanif Mohammad in 1964 — to score a century on a debut Test tour of Australia. **Najmul Hossain Shanto** supported him with **84**, and the pair anchored a total that reached **351 for 6** by stumps. Bangladesh lost some late wickets but **Mehidy Hasan Miraz (32 not out)** and **Hasan Mahmud (13 not out)** dug in through the final overs to see the team safely to the close. Having trailed by 102 runs at the end of day one, Bangladesh now lead Australia by **153 runs** with four wickets in hand — a complete reversal of fortunes inside a single day's play.
stories.why_it_matters: This is shaping up as one of the most significant results in Bangladesh's Test history — a team on just its first-ever tour of Australia is now genuinely competing to win a Test match there, something that would have seemed unthinkable before this series.
stories.ripple_effects: A strong result here would boost Bangladesh's standing in the World Test Championship 2025-2027 cycle and add pressure on other established Test nations who have historically dominated tours of Australia. It also raises Tanzid Hasan's profile as a batter to watch heading into future series.
stories.why_now: This is the direct continuation of day one's play, where Bangladesh's bowling attack had already set up the position by bowling Australia out cheaply.
stories.watch_next: Whether Bangladesh can extend their lead further on day three and set Australia a genuinely challenging target to chase in the fourth innings.

key_terms.definition: A batter's first-ever score of 100 or more runs in a single innings of a Test match.

stories.the_lesson: In Test cricket, a single day's batting can completely flip the balance of a match — momentum built over one innings by one or two players can turn a losing position into a winning one far faster than most other sports allow.

stories.title: Bangladesh push Australia to the brink in Darwin as Starc and Miraz clash on a tense day two
key_points: Australia trail Bangladesh by **153 runs** at stumps on day two in Darwin.
**Tanzid Hasan Tamim's** history-making innings anchored Bangladesh's dominant day.
**Mitchell Starc** and **Mehidy Miraz** exchanged words after Starc accused Miraz of blocking his follow-through.
Australia lost **three wickets** in the final session — a fourth chance went down when Cameron Green dropped a catch.
It is a rare position of real control for Bangladesh in a Test match on Australian soil.
stories.background: Bangladesh have historically struggled badly on tours of Australia, where fast, bouncy pitches have traditionally favoured the host attack. Darwin, hosting this Test, is a newer and less familiar venue on the international circuit, adding an extra layer of unpredictability. Openers like Tanzid Hasan Tamim have been central to a slow but real improvement in Bangladesh's Test batting depth in recent years, even as results away from home remained difficult.
stories.what_happened: On day two of the first Test in Darwin, Bangladesh took firm control, with opener **Tanzid Hasan Tamim** producing a history-making innings that made batting look straightforward against the Australian attack for most of the day. By stumps, **Australia trailed by 153 runs**, having lost three wickets in the final session — and it would have been four had **Cameron Green** not put down a catch on the last ball of the day. Tensions boiled over during the day when **Mitchell Starc** accused Bangladesh's **Mehidy Miraz** of deliberately blocking his follow-through path, with the two exchanging words on the field after a long, hard session for the home bowlers.
stories.why_it_matters: Bangladesh dominating a day of Test cricket on Australian soil is genuinely rare — it's the kind of result that can shift a team's belief about competing away from home, not just this series but going forward.
stories.ripple_effects: If Bangladesh can convert this position into victory or a strong draw, it would rank among their best overseas Test results in years and add pressure on Australia's bowling attack heading into the rest of the home summer. The Starc-Miraz friction is also likely to draw match-referee attention if it continues into later days.
stories.why_now: This is simply the live state of an ongoing Test match, with day two producing the most dramatic passage of play so far in the series.
stories.watch_next: Watch day three to see whether Bangladesh can extend their lead further and whether Australia's bowlers can find a way back into the match.
stories.the_lesson: In Test cricket, momentum built over a single session can flip the entire complexion of a match — which is part of why the format rewards patience and can punish teams that don't respect a tiring bowling attack.

stories.title: India will play their 600th Test — the first Asian team to reach the milestone — as the Sri Lanka series opens at Galle
key_points: India become the **first Asian team**, and only the **third team ever**, to play **600 Tests**.
The Galle Test is also the **50th Test match** ever played at that ground — a first for any Asian venue.
Captain **Shubman Gill** called leading the side in this Test a **'huge honour and privilege.'**
India's squad includes **Auqib Nabi**, uncapped, called up after **Jasprit Bumrah** was ruled out injured.
The first of two Tests runs **August 15–19** at Galle International Stadium.
stories.background: Only England and Australia had previously reached 600 Test matches — a mark of just how long and central those two nations have been to the format since Test cricket began in 1877. India, despite a huge domestic cricket culture, is reaching this landmark later because Test cricket globally has always been dominated in volume by England and Australia's early head start. Galle, meanwhile, has become one of world cricket's most picturesque and historic grounds since Sri Lanka started hosting Tests there, set beside the Indian Ocean next to a centuries-old Dutch fort.
stories.what_happened: India's first Test against Sri Lanka, starting **August 15** at Galle International Stadium, will be India's **600th Test match overall**, making them the first Asian side and just the third team in history — after England and Australia — to reach that number. The match is also the **50th Test hosted at Galle**, the first Asian venue to reach that mark. Captain **Shubman Gill**, who described the milestone as a 'huge honour,' will lead a squad that includes vice-captain KL Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Rishabh Pant, Ravindra Jadeja, and uncapped seamer **Auqib Nabi**, who earned a shock maiden call-up after **Jasprit Bumrah** was ruled out with a knee injury. Sri Lanka will field a 16-member squad led by Dhananjaya de Silva, with Kamindu Mendis as his deputy. The two-match series runs through late August.
stories.why_it_matters: Test cricket's slower, longer format is widely seen as the sport's most demanding and prestigious, so reaching 600 matches is a marker of a cricketing nation's staying power in the format — significant for India as it continues to balance a red-ball program against the far more lucrative T20 leagues that dominate the modern game.
stories.ripple_effects: A strong showing at a landmark match adds momentum to India's push to reach the World Test Championship final, a stated goal for the team under Gill. For Auqib Nabi, a debut here — the first Test cricketer from Jammu and Kashmir if he plays — would be a significant, symbolically important moment for the region's cricket development.
stories.why_now: The milestone lines up with the start of a previously-scheduled bilateral series, not a specially arranged event — it's simply where India's Test-match count happened to land.
stories.watch_next: Watch whether Auqib Nabi is handed his Test debut in the XI, and how India's much-changed pace attack performs without Bumrah.
stories.the_lesson: Longevity in the toughest version of a sport is its own kind of achievement — separate from and sometimes at odds with short-term commercial success, since the two rewards (prestige versus revenue) don't always point in the same direction.

stories.title: Pakistan slip to 261 behind on day two of their final Test warm-up before the England series
key_points: Pakistan closed day two trailing by **261 runs** in their three-day warm-up match at Beckenham.
Openers **Imam-ul-Haq (26*) and Azan Awais (15*)** were unbeaten at the close.
The match is Pakistan's **last hit-out** before the first Test at **Headingley on August 19**.
The fixture was **shortened from four days to three** due to player availability.
Pakistan had bowled the **PCC Select XI** out for **305** on day one.
stories.background: Before a Test series, touring teams typically play one or more 'warm-up' matches against a mix of county and invitational players to get used to English conditions — the pitch, the weather, and the swinging ball — before the real series begins. Pakistan are preparing for a three-match Test series against England that starts **August 19 at Headingley in Leeds**, their first assignment under a series that also marks a fresh start for England, who are being led by a returning captain, Joe Root, this series. This particular warm-up fixture, against a **Professional County Club (PCC) Select XI** at Beckenham, was trimmed from four days to three because of player availability.
stories.what_happened: On day two of their three-day warm-up match at Beckenham, Pakistan's top order struggled to make inroads, with the side closing the day trailing by **261 runs** after the PCC Select XI's first-innings total of **305**. Openers **Imam-ul-Haq (26 not out)** and **Azan Awais (15 not out)** were still at the crease at the close of play, having avoided losing a wicket so far in Pakistan's reply. On day one, Pakistan's bowlers — sharing six wickets between them — had restricted the PCC Select XI to 305 all out. With the match reduced to three days because of player availability, day three (August 15) is Pakistan's last chance to build some batting form and rhythm before the series opener.
stories.why_it_matters: This is Pakistan's final tune-up before a three-match series that will shape their World Test Championship campaign, and a slow start with the bat here raises questions about their top order's readiness for the moving ball in English conditions.
stories.ripple_effects: A shaky warm-up performance could influence Pakistan's batting order or team selection for the first Test, and it feeds into broader pre-series narratives about whether Pakistan's batters can cope with England's bowling attack, including a recalled Brydon Carse.
stories.why_now: This is the direct lead-in to Pakistan's opening Test against England, which starts in five days.
stories.watch_next: Watch how Pakistan's top order performs on day three, and whether captain Shan Masood or the coaching staff make any late adjustments before the Headingley Test.

key_terms.definition: A practice fixture, usually against a scratch or county side, that touring international teams play to adjust to local conditions before a series begins.

stories.the_lesson: Preparation matches matter less for the result and more for what they reveal — a team's form and confidence heading into a big series often shows up in these low-stakes games first.

stories.title: Bangladesh claws back to 175 for 2 on day two in Darwin, trailing Australia by just 23 runs
key_points: Bangladesh reached **175/2** after 50 overs on day two, having bowled Australia out for **198** in their first innings
**Mominul Haque (35 not out)** and **Tanzid Hasan (32 not out)** are steering a fightback that has trimmed the deficit to just **23 runs**
The platform follows **Hasan Mahmud's career-best 6 for 55**, which skittled Australia's first innings on day one
This is Bangladesh's **first-ever Test tour of Australia**, ending a 23-year wait for a red-ball series Down Under
Australia's **Mitchell Starc** became Test cricket's most successful left-arm bowler during the innings, passing Rangana Herath
stories.background: Bangladesh's tour of Australia is historic in itself — this is the first time the team has played a Test series in Australia, 23 years after first joining the small group of nations with Test status. The match is being played in Darwin, a venue known for hot, humid conditions that can behave differently to Australia's more familiar southern grounds. Bangladesh went into day one as heavy underdogs against an Australian side that includes veteran fast bowler Mitchell Starc, one of the most successful bowlers in the format's history.
stories.what_happened: On day one, Bangladesh's bowlers bundled Australia out for just 198, with fast bowler Hasan Mahmud claiming a career-best 6 for 55, and the tourists closed the day at 96 for 1 in reply. On day two, Bangladesh continued building on that platform, reaching 175 for 2 after 50 overs with Mominul Haque unbeaten on 35 and Tanzid Hasan unbeaten on 32, cutting the deficit to Australia's total to just 23 runs. During Australia's innings, veteran fast bowler Mitchell Starc passed Sri Lanka's Rangana Herath to become the most successful left-arm bowler in Test cricket history.
stories.why_it_matters: A first-innings lead, or even a small deficit, would be a landmark result for Bangladesh on their first-ever Test visit to Australia — a result that would rank among the biggest upsets of their Test history if it holds.
stories.ripple_effects: A strong showing here would boost Bangladesh's case for more regular Test tours to major cricket nations and lift their position in the World Test Championship standings. It would also raise fresh questions about Australia's depth outside their home comfort zone in more traditional conditions.
stories.why_now: The match is live and in progress, with day two's play having just concluded — the story is developing in real time as the tourists close in on Australia's total.
stories.watch_next: Whether Bangladesh can push past Australia's total of 198 and build a first-innings lead when play resumes on day three.
stories.the_lesson: In Test cricket, momentum built with the ball on day one can carry straight into a batting fightback on day two — a good bowling performance often sets up the platform for an unlikely result.

**Shubman Gill** has been declared fit to captain the side after a finger scare in the warm-up match
**Auqib Nabi**, 26, earns his maiden India call-up after taking **104 wickets** across his last two Ranji Trophy seasons

Bumrah, India's premier fast bowler, has been carefully managed through injuries in recent months, while allrounder Ravindra Jadeja's fitness has also been closely watched heading into this tour.

A poor start could also increase pressure on India's position in the WTC standings.
stories.why_now: The squad announcement comes just two days before the series opener, giving the team its final answers on fitness and selection right before departure.
stories.watch_next: How Auqib Nabi performs in his Test debut at Galle, and whether Bumrah is fit to return for the second Test in Colombo.

stories.title: Scotland thump Canada by 170 runs in Dundee rematch to boost their 2027 World Cup qualification hopes
key_points: Scotland beat Canada by **170 runs** in Dundee, posting **347/7** before bowling Canada out for just **177**.
Left-armer **Lyle Robertson** starred with **6 wickets for 52 runs**, earning Player of the Match.
The result comes just days after Scotland edged the same opponent by a much tighter **9 runs** in an earlier meeting.

The two sides had already met earlier this month in a tight 9-run Scotland win, making this rematch a chance for Scotland to build a bigger points cushion.
stories.what_happened: Scotland posted a commanding **347 for 7** batting first at Forthill in Dundee, then bowled out Canada for just **177**, winning by **170 runs**. Left-arm bowler Lyle Robertson was the standout performer, taking **6 wickets for 52 runs** to earn Player of the Match honours. The comprehensive win comes just a week after the two sides met in a far closer contest, which Scotland won by only 9 runs (281/7 to Canada's 272), underlining how much more dominant this second meeting was.
stories.why_it_matters: Every match in the World Cup League 2 carries direct weight toward 2027 World Cup qualification for associate nations, where net run-rate and win margins — not just results — can decide who advances.
stories.ripple_effects: The big win boosts Scotland's net run-rate as well as their points tally, strengthening their position in the qualification table relative to Canada and other associate nations in the league.

stories.title: India cruise past Sri Lanka Cricket XI in their Galle warm-up as bowling coach Morkel backs KL Rahul to anchor the Test series

KL Rahul, a senior and experienced batter, is the only player left in India's current squad who also featured on India's previous Test tour of Sri Lanka in 2017, making his knowledge of local conditions unusually valuable to a squad otherwise light on recent experience there. stories.what_happened: India opened their Sri Lanka tour with a comfortable **six-wicket win over a Sri Lanka Cricket XI** in a three-day warm-up match, built around an unbeaten **142 from Devdutt Padikkal**. In the build-up, India's bowling coach Morne Morkel spoke publicly about the value KL Rahul brings to the squad, highlighting his experience and his role in helping younger players adjust to conditions in Sri Lanka. stories.title: BCCI seeks the Indian government's go-ahead before confirming a Bangladesh tour, as cricket ties stay strained
key_points: BCCI says it will approach the **Indian government** for formal clearance before confirming a tour of Bangladesh
Tensions began in **January 2026** when BCCI asked KKR to release Bangladeshi bowler Mustafizur Rahman from the IPL
Bangladesh's board (BCB) then **refused to travel to India** for the 2026 T20 World Cup, citing security advice
A recent visit by **BCB president Tamim Iqbal** to the BCCI's Bengaluru academy has revived hopes for the tour
The series was originally set for **August 2025** before being deferred to **September 2026**
stories.background: Cricket ties between India and Bangladesh soured amid the political turmoil in Bangladesh under its interim government led by Muhammad Yunus, feeding into a broader chill in bilateral relations. The flashpoint came when BCCI, citing violence against religious minorities in Bangladesh, asked Kolkata Knight Riders to release Bangladeshi pace bowler Mustafizur Rahman from their IPL 2026 squad — a request Bangladesh's board answered days later by pulling its national team out of traveling to India for the 2026 T20 World Cup over security concerns. Since then, ties have shown signs of thawing under new Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
stories.what_happened: BCCI sources say the board has locked in a proposed window for a six-match tour of Bangladesh but will not confirm it until it receives formal approval from the Indian government — standard practice for tours to countries where diplomatic sensitivities are in play. This follows a visit by BCB president Tamim Iqbal to the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, which cricket officials on both sides described as a positive step toward normalizing relations. The tour, originally scheduled for August 2025, was deferred by mutual agreement to September 2026 after the earlier diplomatic rupture.
stories.why_it_matters: Cricket between India and Bangladesh is not just sport — it has become a visible barometer of the two countries' broader political relationship, and a canceled or confirmed tour sends a real diplomatic signal beyond the pitch. Government sign-off requirements show how closely India treats sports diplomacy as an extension of foreign policy when relations are fragile.
stories.ripple_effects: A confirmed tour would be read as a genuine thaw in India-Bangladesh relations and give both boards' broadcast and sponsorship revenues a lift; a further delay or cancellation would be read as ties remaining fragile. Player availability and IPL contracts for Bangladeshi cricketers could also remain a flashpoint depending on how relations evolve.
stories.why_now: The tour window needs to be locked in soon given the September 2026 target date, forcing BCCI to seek government clearance now.
stories.watch_next: Watch for the Indian government's formal response and whether BCCI and BCB announce confirmed fixtures for the September window.
stories.the_lesson: When diplomatic relations between two countries sour, even seemingly unrelated institutions — like national cricket boards — end up needing government sign-off, because sport rarely stays separate from politics for long.

stories.title: India names Shubman Gill to captain the Sri Lanka Tests, with Bumrah and Jadeja's returns still hanging on fitness
key_points: BCCI named its **15-man Test squad** for the two-match Sri Lanka series, starting **August 15** in Galle
**Shubman Gill** continues as captain, with **KL Rahul** as vice-captain
**Ravindra Jadeja** returns after being rested for the Afghanistan series in June
**Jasprit Bumrah**'s spot is contested — reports conflict on whether he's fully cleared or still assessing his knee
**Auqib Nabi**, a 26-year-old pacer from Jammu and Kashmir, gets a maiden call-up after **104 wickets** in two Ranji seasons
stories.background: India's Test side has been managing a wave of injuries through the middle of 2026, with fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah's fitness in particular being carefully managed by the BCCI's medical team since a knee issue first flared up around the T20 World Cup. The two-Test series against Sri Lanka — the first Test in Galle from August 15-19, the second in Colombo from August 23-27 — comes as India also manages the workload of veterans like Ravindra Jadeja, who sat out the Afghanistan series in June.
stories.what_happened: BCCI's selection committee announced the squad on **Tuesday**, confirming **Shubman Gill** as Test captain and **KL Rahul** in the leadership group as vice-captain. Ravindra Jadeja returns to the squad after his rest period, and uncapped domestic performer **Auqib Nabi** earns his first India call-up on the back of 104 wickets across his last two Ranji Trophy seasons. Jasprit Bumrah's status remains genuinely unsettled: some reports say he has been named in the squad but will only play once he clears a fitness test with the BCCI's Centre of Excellence, while other reports say he has already been ruled out and replaced by Nabi. India also has a four-day practice match in Colombo before the series to help assess player fitness.
stories.why_it_matters: Bumrah is India's premier fast bowler and a genuine match-winner in Test cricket — his availability alone can swing a series, so his uncertain status is the single biggest storyline heading into the tour. The squad announcement also confirms India's leadership continuity under Gill after a period of speculation about his own fitness.
stories.ripple_effects: If Bumrah is unavailable, India's pace attack leans more heavily on Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna, changing the tactical balance against a Sri Lankan side that will target any inexperience in the bowling unit. A debut for Nabi also puts a spotlight on India's depth pipeline outside the usual metro cricket centres.
stories.why_now: The squad had to be finalized ahead of the team's departure and a four-day warm-up match in Colombo before the first Test begins August 15.
stories.watch_next: Watch for confirmation of Bumrah's final fitness clearance before the first Test XI is named in Galle.

key_terms.definition: India's premier domestic first-class cricket tournament, played between state teams and the traditional pathway for players to earn national selection.

stories.the_lesson: In sports as in business, uncertainty about your most important asset (here, a star player's fitness) often matters more for planning than any single confirmed fact — teams have to build contingency plans around doubt, not just certainty.

stories.title: Mitchell Starc becomes Test cricket's most successful left-arm bowler ever, passing Rangana Herath
key_points: Starc reached **434 Test wickets**, passing Sri Lanka's **Rangana Herath (433)** to become the most successful left-arm bowler in Test history.
He got there by dismissing Bangladesh opener **Shadman Islam** during the historic **Darwin Test**.
The milestone came in his **106th Test**, and fell on **International Left-Handers Day** (August 13).
Starc is now **level with Kapil Dev** on the all-time wicket-takers list, and just **six behind Dale Steyn's 439** for the top ten overall.
stories.background: Mitchell Starc has been Australia's frontline left-arm fast bowler for over a decade, known for swinging the new ball and reverse-swinging the old one. Left-arm bowlers face a quirk regardless of pace or style: there have simply been far fewer of them across cricket history than right-arm bowlers, which makes elite career wicket tallies rarer among them. Sri Lankan left-arm spinner **Rangana Herath** had held the left-arm wicket-taking record with 433 dismissals since his retirement. Starc reached the milestone during Australia's landmark first-ever home Test against Bangladesh, a fixture Bangladesh waited 23 years to secure.
stories.what_happened: During day two of the Australia-Bangladesh Test in Darwin, Mitchell Starc dismissed opener Shadman Islam to take his **434th Test wicket**, moving past Rangana Herath's **433** to become the leading left-arm bowler in Test cricket history. The milestone arrived in Starc's **106th Test appearance** and, fittingly, on **International Left-Handers Day**. The achievement also puts him level with India great **Kapil Dev** on the all-time wicket-takers list, and within six wickets of South Africa's **Dale Steyn (439)** for a place in the game's top ten leading wicket-takers overall, regardless of arm or bowling style.
stories.why_it_matters: This cements Starc's place among the greatest fast bowlers of his generation, and highlights how rare genuinely elite left-arm bowling careers are — there have been far fewer standout left-armers across Test history than right-armers, making a tally like this especially significant.
stories.ripple_effects: The milestone adds to the storyline of Australia's dominant bowling attack during a historic tour, and will likely fuel more discussion about where Starc ultimately ranks among all-time greats as he continues closing in on the top-ten wicket-takers list.
stories.why_now: It happened live during play on day two of the ongoing Darwin Test, cricket's first-ever meeting between Australia and Bangladesh on Australian soil.
stories.watch_next: Whether Starc can close the six-wicket gap to Dale Steyn's 439 before this series ends, and how far Australia push their advantage in the rest of the Darwin Test.

key_terms.definition: A bowler who delivers the ball with their left hand — rarer than right-arm bowlers across cricket history, which makes high career wicket tallies among left-armers especially notable.

stories.the_lesson: Longevity and consistency compound — Starc's record didn't come from one standout spell, but from turning up and taking wickets across 106 Tests over more than a decade.

stories.title: Scotland and Canada clash again in Dundee with 2027 World Cup qualification hopes on the line
key_points: Scotland and Canada are playing their second meeting in a week in the **ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2**, this time in Dundee
Scotland sit **2nd** in the League 2 table with 38 points from 32 matches; Canada are **5th** with 20 points from 20 games
The two teams last met on **August 7**, when Scotland won by 9 runs in a high-scoring game (281/7 vs 272)
League 2 results feed directly into qualification for the **2027 Cricket World Cup** — making every match here count for both sides
Scotland reached **267/4** in their innings today, with Michael Jones unbeaten on 41, as they push to extend their points lead
stories.background: The **ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2** is a multi-year one-day international league for cricket's second tier of nations, running from 2023 to 2027. It's a key step on the qualification pathway toward the **2027 Cricket World Cup**, so results here have real stakes even though the teams involved — Scotland, Canada, Namibia, UAE, USA, and others — rarely make global headlines. Scotland and Canada have faced each other repeatedly in this cycle, most recently on August 7 in a tight 9-run Scotland win, and today's rematch in Dundee is part of the same tightly-fought race for qualification points.
stories.what_happened: Playing at their home ground of Forthill in Dundee, **Scotland batted first** against Canada in the 126th match of the League 2 cycle. At the time of writing, Scotland had reached **267/4**, with batter Michael Jones unbeaten on 41 and wicketkeeper Matthew Cross also not out, building a total aimed at extending their strong position near the top of the table. Scotland currently sit second in the League 2 standings with 38 points from 32 matches (16 wins), while Canada are fifth with 20 points from 20 games and need a strong finish to stay in contention for a World Cup Qualifier spot.
stories.why_it_matters: For cricket's smaller nations, League 2 matches like this one are often the difference between reaching a global tournament and missing out entirely — there's no broadcast deal or star-driven hype, but the competitive stakes for these teams' World Cup dreams are as real as any bigger series.
stories.ripple_effects: A strong Scotland performance here widens their cushion near the top of the table and pushes Canada further from a qualification spot, shaping the field that will eventually contest the 2027 World Cup Qualifier tournament.
stories.why_now: This is the second Scotland-Canada meeting inside a week as both teams pack in League 2 fixtures before the qualification window closes.
stories.watch_next: The final result of today's match, and how it shifts the League 2 points table with the qualification race intensifying.

key_terms.definition: A multi-year one-day international league among cricket's associate and lower-ranked nations that determines qualification paths to the Cricket World Cup.

stories.the_lesson: Sport's biggest stakes aren't always found in its biggest games — for teams outside cricket's traditional powers, a routine-looking league match can carry the same win-or-miss-the-World-Cup weight as a marquee fixture.

stories.title: Pakistan get a fitness boost as Shan Masood returns to training before the England Tests
key_points: Pakistan opener **Shan Masood** has returned to training, raising hopes he'll be fit for the first Test against England
Masood injured a finger during the opening Test of Pakistan's series against the **West Indies** in the Caribbean
He missed the second Test — which Pakistan still won, ending a **three-year wait** for an away Test victory
The Pakistan Test series against England begins **August 19 at Leeds**, with three Tests forming part of the 2025–2027 World Test Championship cycle
Pakistan currently sit **8th** in the World Test Championship standings, hoping this tour continues their recent resurgence
stories.background: Pakistan's Test team, now led by captain **Babar Azam**, has been in the middle of a tour of England that includes a three-day warm-up match against a Professional County Club Select XI before the main event: a **three-Test series** starting at Leeds on August 19, followed by Lord's and Birmingham. This series counts toward the **2025–2027 ICC World Test Championship**, the two-year league that determines which two teams reach the WTC final. Pakistan enter the tour off the back of a genuinely good result — beating the West Indies away for the first time in three years — but that win came with a cost: opening batter Shan Masood picked up a finger injury in the first Test of that series.
stories.what_happened: Masood, who missed the second Test of the West Indies series because of his finger injury, **resumed training with the Pakistan squad at Beckenham** this week, ahead of the team's three-day tour match there against a Professional County Club Select XI running August 13–15. His return to full training is being read as a positive sign for his availability for the first Test against England in Leeds on August 19. Pakistan's touring squad includes Babar Azam as captain, alongside Mohammad Rizwan, Saud Shakeel, Imam-ul-Haq, and a bowling attack featuring Mohammad Abbas, Aamir Jamal, and Sajid Khan.
stories.why_it_matters: Masood is one of Pakistan's most experienced Test openers, and having him fit to face the new ball against England's attack — especially at Leeds, a ground known for helping seam bowlers — materially improves Pakistan's chances in a series they'll want to use to build on their West Indies form.
stories.ripple_effects: A fit top order gives Pakistan a stronger platform against an England side under new Test captain Joe Root, who takes over from the retired Ben Stokes for this series — meaning both teams are carrying some uncertainty into the opener.
stories.why_now: Masood's return to training happened this week, directly ahead of Pakistan's final warm-up match before the Leeds Test begins.
stories.watch_next: Whether Masood is passed fit and included in Pakistan's XI for the first Test at Leeds on August 19.

key_terms.definition: A two-year league where all Test-playing nations play a set number of series against each other; the top two teams meet in a final to decide the overall Test champion.

stories.the_lesson: In Test cricket, a team's form often hinges as much on which players are fit to play as on raw skill — a single injured opener can change how an entire series is approached.

stories.title: India's injury crunch deepens: Sai Sudharsan ruled out of the Sri Lanka Tests with a toe fracture, and captain Shubman Gill is now under an injury cloud too

thread.previously: When India named its 15-man Test squad for Sri Lanka, Jadeja returned from injury but Jasprit Bumrah was ruled out; Sai Sudharsan and Bumrah's spots had been made conditional on fitness clearance, and Gill's own earlier finger injury was reported as resolved.
thread.changed: Sudharsan has now failed that fitness test and is officially ruled out with a toe stress fracture, with no replacement yet named — and captain Shubman Gill has picked up a new, separate injury, hurting his right ring finger in training in Colombo just before the series starts.

key_points: **Sai Sudharsan** is ruled out of the two-Test Sri Lanka series with a **toe stress fracture**.
He had been given a conditional spot pending fitness clearance from the BCCI's **Centre of Excellence (CoE)** — he didn't recover in time.
No replacement for Sudharsan has been named yet, and he did not travel with the squad to Sri Lanka.
Captain **Shubman Gill** is now also under an injury cloud after hurting his **right ring finger** in a training session in Colombo.
The series starts **August 15 in Galle**, with the second Test in **Colombo from August 23**.
stories.background: India named its Test squad for the Sri Lanka tour with some fitness question marks already attached: Sudharsan and Bumrah's places were both conditional on medical clearance after recent injuries, and Bumrah ultimately missed out. Sudharsan picked up a **toe stress fracture** — a small crack in the bone from repeated stress rather than a single impact — after returning from India A's tour of Sri Lanka in July, and had been at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence trying to recover in time.
stories.what_happened: India batter **Sai Sudharsan** has been ruled out of the upcoming two-Test series in Sri Lanka because of a **toe stress fracture** that hasn't healed enough for him to be declared fit. He had been named in the initial 15-man squad, but his selection — like Bumrah's — was conditional on medical clearance from the BCCI's Centre of Excellence, and he ultimately failed to get it in time; he did not travel with the squad and **no replacement has been named yet**. Adding to India's pre-series injury concerns, Test captain **Shubman Gill** is now also under an injury cloud after hurting his **right ring finger** during a training session in Colombo — a new issue, separate from an earlier finger problem that had already been reported resolved. The two-Test series begins **August 15 in Galle**, with the second Test starting **August 23** at the SSC in Colombo.
stories.why_it_matters: India already lost Bumrah, its premier fast bowler, to injury for this series, and now loses a top-order batting option too — while its own captain is battling a fresh knock just two days before the first ball, raising real questions about the depth and readiness of India's squad heading into a series against a Sri Lanka team playing at home.
stories.ripple_effects: Selectors will need to name a replacement batter quickly, likely reshaping India's top order for the series. If Gill's finger issue worsens, India could even face a late captaincy or personnel change right before the first Test, adding pressure on vice-captain KL Rahul to be ready to step in.
stories.why_now: The news broke just two days before the series opener on August 15, the point by which players' conditional fitness clearances had to be finalized one way or the other.
stories.watch_next: Whether India names a replacement for Sudharsan before the August 15 first Test, and whether Gill is passed fit to lead the side in Galle.

key_terms.definition: A small crack in a bone caused by repeated impact or overuse, rather than a single injury — common in athletes and often slow to heal.

stories.the_lesson: Conditional squad selections — 'in the team pending fitness' — are a real risk, not a formality; when a team leans on several players clearing medical checks at once, injury depth becomes the deciding factor in how competitive the side actually is on day one.
